questions.prompt: According to the law of demand, when price rises, quantity demanded…
questions.explanation: Ceteris paribus, a higher price means a lower quantity demanded.

questions.prompt: A drought destroys much of the bean harvest. What happens to the equilibrium price of beans?
questions.explanation: Supply decreases (shifts left), so equilibrium price rises and quantity falls.

questions.prompt: Using the same equations, find the equilibrium quantity.
If the market price is **below** equilibrium, there will be…
questions.explanation: At a low price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between a movement along a demand curve and a shift of the demand curve. Give one cause of each.
questions.marking_guide: 1: movement = change in quantity demanded caused by change in the good's own price. 1: correct example (price rise/fall). 1: shift = change in demand at every price caused by a non-price factor. 1: correct example (income, tastes, price of substitutes/complements, population, expectations).
questions.explanation: Own-price changes move you along the curve; other factors shift the whole curve.
